orbitSummary: Low Earth orbit, about 500 km up. One orbit takes ~95 minutes; ground stations see it only a few times a day.
description: A small, low-cost satellite: one of each unit (no redundancy), 1-3 year life.

subsystems.name: Structure & Mechanisms
subsystems.description: The skeleton: carries every unit through launch vibration and holds the satellite together in orbit. A CubeSat's outer size is fixed by the CubeSat Design Specification so it fits the launch dispenser.

slots.name: 3U structure
slots.why: Rails, frames and end plates. Must match the CubeSat standard: 100 x 100 x 340.5 mm.

variants.name: Aluminium 3U frame
variants.description: Machined aluminium alloy: the common, robust choice.

variants.name: Lightweight 3U frame
variants.description: Thinner walls save mass for payload, with less stiffness margin.

slots.name: Deployment switches
slots.why: Pressed by the dispenser's walls; they keep the satellite completely switched off until it is released.

variants.name: 2 rail-end switches
variants.description: Spring plungers in two rail feet.

slots.name: Remove-before-flight pin
slots.why: Keeps the power off while people handle the satellite on the ground. Pulled out just before integration into the dispenser.

variants.name: RBF pin
variants.description: Removable pin through a switch on the open side.

slots.name: Hold-down and release mechanism
slots.why: Holds the deployable wings closed during launch, then burns a restraint line to free them.

variants.name: Burn-wire release (2)
variants.description: A heated wire melts a Dyneema line that holds each wing.

subsystems.name: Payload
subsystems.description: The reason the satellite exists. Choose the mission first: it decides how precisely you must point, how much data you send down and how much power you need.

slots.name: Main payload
slots.why: What your mission measures or does.

variants.name: Earth observation camera
variants.description: Takes pictures of the Earth. Needs fine pointing and a fast downlink, so it triggers reaction wheels, a star tracker and an S-band transmitter.

parameters.label: Lens baffle length
parameters.help: A longer baffle blocks more stray sunlight.

variants.name: Space-weather sensor
variants.description: Measures particles and fields around the satellite. Needs only coarse pointing and a little data.

subsystems.name: Electrical Power (EPS)
subsystems.description: Makes, stores and distributes electricity. In LEO the satellite is in Earth's shadow for about a third of every 95-minute orbit, so the battery charges and discharges thousands of times a year.

slots.name: Solar panels
slots.why: Turn sunlight into electricity, the only power source in orbit.

variants.name: Body panels + 2 deployable wings
variants.description: Adds two hinged wings that open after release, roughly tripling the sunlit area.

parameters.label: Wing opening angle
parameters.help: Tilt the wings to change which way their cells face.

variants.name: Body-mounted panels (3 faces)
variants.description: Cells glued directly onto three faces. Simple and robust, but limited area.

parameters.label: Cell rows per panel
parameters.help: More rows of cells = more power, until the panel is full.

slots.name: Battery pack
slots.why: Powers the satellite through every eclipse and through peaks such as radio transmissions.

variants.name: 2-cell Li-ion pack
variants.description: 18650 cells with protection circuit.

variants.name: 4-cell Li-ion pack
variants.description: More energy for longer eclipses and power-hungry payloads.

slots.name: Power control & distribution board
slots.why: Tracks the solar arrays' best operating point, charges the battery and switches power to each unit.

variants.name: EPS board with MPPT
variants.description: Peak-power tracking, battery charger, 3.3 V / 5 V rails, 8 switched outputs.

subsystems.name: On-board Computer (OBC)
subsystems.description: The satellite's brain: runs its modes, stores data between ground-station passes and protects itself with a watchdog that restarts it if it hangs.

slots.name: Flight computer
slots.why: Executes commands, collects telemetry, runs the attitude control and fault handling.

variants.name: Flight computer (microcontroller)
variants.description: Low-power radiation-tolerant microcontroller board.

variants.name: Flight computer + FPGA processor
variants.description: Adds an FPGA for on-board image processing and compression.

slots.name: Data storage
slots.why: Keeps telemetry and payload data until the next pass over a ground station.

variants.name: 8 GB flash
variants.description: Industrial flash memory.

variants.name: 64 GB flash
variants.description: For image-heavy missions.

subsystems.name: Communications (TT&C)
subsystems.description: Telemetry, tracking and command: how the satellite talks to the ground. In LEO a ground station only sees the satellite for a few passes of about 10 minutes per day.

slots.name: UHF transceiver
slots.why: Receives commands and sends telemetry and a beacon.

variants.name: UHF transceiver
variants.description: Half-duplex radio, 9.6 kbit/s.

variants.name: VHF/UHF transceiver
variants.description: Uplink on VHF, downlink on UHF; avoids interference between the two.

slots.name: UHF antenna
slots.why: Coiled tape-spring elements; the CubeSat standard requires waiting after release before deploying them and before transmitting.

variants.name: Turnstile (4 elements)
variants.description: Near-omnidirectional coverage in any attitude.

parameters.label: Element length
parameters.help: A quarter-wavelength at ~435 MHz is about 0.17 m.

variants.name: Dipole (2 elements)
variants.description: Simpler; has nulls along its axis.

slots.name: S-band transmitter + patch antenna
slots.why: High-rate downlink for large data volumes.

variants.name: S-band transmitter
variants.description: Up to ~2 Mbit/s downlink.

slots.conditionText: your camera payload produces a lot of image data

slots.name: GNSS receiver
slots.why: Gives the satellite its own position and accurate time.

variants.name: GNSS receiver + patch
variants.description: Small GPS/Galileo receiver.

subsystems.name: Attitude Control (ADCS)
subsystems.description: Measures and controls which way the satellite points. After release it tumbles; the first job is to stop the tumbling (detumble) using the Earth's magnetic field, which is strong in LEO.

slots.name: Magnetometer
slots.why: Measures the Earth's magnetic field: needed to detumble with magnetorquers.

variants.name: 3-axis magnetometer
variants.description: Small chip on the ADCS board.

slots.name: Magnetorquers
slots.why: Electromagnets that push against Earth's field: detumbling and momentum dumping. Work well only in LEO.

variants.name: 3 torque rods
variants.description: Copper coils on ferromagnetic cores.

parameters.label: Rod thickness
parameters.help: Thicker rods give a stronger magnetic dipole.

slots.name: Coarse Sun sensors
slots.why: Find the Sun from any attitude: used for power-safe pointing.

variants.name: 6 coarse Sun sensors
variants.description: Photodiodes on every face.

slots.name: Gyro / IMU
slots.why: Measures how fast the satellite rotates.

variants.name: MEMS IMU
variants.description: Gyros + accelerometers on a chip.

slots.name: Reaction wheels
slots.why: Spinning flywheels: speeding one up turns the satellite the other way. Needed for fine pointing.

variants.name: 3 wheels (shown cut away)
variants.description: Housings opened so you can see the flywheels.

parameters.label: Flywheel radius
parameters.help: A bigger flywheel stores more momentum but weighs more.

variants.name: 3 wheels (sealed housings)
variants.description: As flown: each flywheel sealed in its housing.

slots.name: Star tracker
slots.why: Camera that recognises star patterns: the most accurate attitude sensor.

variants.name: Nano star tracker
variants.description: Arc-second class accuracy.

subsystems.name: Thermal Control
subsystems.description: Keeps every unit inside its temperature limits. On a CubeSat this is mostly passive: surface finishes set how much sunlight is absorbed and how much heat is radiated.

slots.name: Surface finishes
slots.why: Coatings and tapes that set the overall temperature balance.

variants.name: Black anodize + white paint
variants.description: Standard finishes on frame and radiating surfaces.

variants.name: Silver thermal tape
variants.description: Reflects more sunlight; runs cooler.

slots.name: Temperature sensors
slots.why: Thermistors report temperatures in telemetry.

variants.name: 8 thermistors
variants.description: On battery, boards and panels.

slots.name: Battery heater
slots.why: Lithium cells must not be charged below about 0 C, so the battery has its own heater.

variants.name: Kapton film heater
variants.description: Thin heater under the battery, thermostat controlled.

subsystems.name: Propulsion
subsystems.description: Optional on a CubeSat in low orbit: air drag brings it down within the deorbit time limit. Needed to change or maintain the orbit, or to dodge debris.

slots.name: Propulsion module
slots.why: Changes the orbit, avoids collisions, speeds up deorbit.

variants.name: Cold-gas module (4 nozzles)
variants.description: Compressed gas through four small nozzles: simple and safe, low total impulse.

parameters.label: Nozzle exit radius
parameters.help: A larger exit (expansion ratio) gets a little more thrust from the same gas.
